milestone.title: mp autopilot spawn-prompt template + harness-extra-flags translation

intent.outcome: When mp autopilot spawns a fresh pane in the herdr workspace, the pane boots with a session-bound system prompt that names the project, the session id, the milestone, the pane's role (which skill to load), the role's explicit `what you cannot do` boundaries, and the lane-notify wire format — so the agent's first context window is grounded in role + contract before any freeform work begins.

problem.description: In M201 cycle 1 and M203, the runner pane's context drift caused it to forget its role boundaries; it fabricated lifecycle state, called `mp reviews pass` directly, and otherwise did what achieved the goal without honoring the role. Skills alone (`mp-runner` etc.) drift in long contexts. The fix is a session-bound system prompt at spawn time (per the simplification conversation): the spawn pipeline renders a template per role that includes project metadata (so the agent knows which project it's driving), the session id (so it can correlate with session.json), the milestone id, the role's `Boundaries` block (in code, not in SKILL.md), and the lane-notify format. Multi-skill load: in 2-pane mode the supervisor pane gets both O and V prompt contents concatenated (or rendered separately) so it carries both contracts. The harness-extra-flags translation turns `role.skill` into the harness-specific flag (opencode's `--skill`, cursor's `--agent`).

in_scope: Render the spawn prompt from a template in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/prompts/spawn.rs` per role. Inputs: session.json (workspace, session id, milestone id, queue position), resolved RoleConfig (model, harness, skill, extras), the per-role `Boundaries` block (hardcoded per role, in code per the locked decision).
Three role templates (O, R, V); the 2-pane supervisor bundle concatenates O + V; 1-pane concatenates O + R + V.

`harness_extra_flags(rc)` translation: opencode → `--skill <name> --model <id>`; cursor → `--agent <name> --model <id>`; pi → equivalent PI config injection. Returns the argv list to append to `herdr agent start`.
Spawn-prompt rendering is pure: same inputs → same prompt. Tested via golden-file fixtures per role + topology.
On spawn, the template is rendered once, written into the session.json `roles.<role>.spawn_prompt_rendered` field for audit, and passed to the herdr spawn call.
out_of_scope: The lane-notify wire format (B2's downstream of the lane's reply messages) — that's C1.
Decision-matrix templates — those land with C3.
Per-role SKILL.md content (the `mp-orchestrator` etc. skills ship as part of a separate track, not under B2).
Harness-side permission policies — out per the simplification decision; the `Boundaries` block in the spawn prompt is the only boundary mechanism at spawn time.

acceptance_criteria.description: Spawn-prompt rendering is deterministic: same RoleConfig + session.json slice → byte-identical prompt string. Golden-file tests cover all three roles in 3-pane, plus the O+V concatenation for 2-pane and O+R+V for 1-pane.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test spawn_prompt_golden --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Each rendered spawn prompt contains project/session/milestone identity, role and skill, explicit role boundaries, M211 task-assignment contract, and the exact `mp autopilot session transition` commands the role must use; prompts never direct agents to edit session.json directly.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test spawn_prompt_contains --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: `harness_extra_flags` returns a documented argv list for opencode, Cursor, and Pi, including exact skill/agent and model translation; unsupported harnesses fail before pane creation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test harness_extra_flags --no-fail-fast exit 0 (8/8 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Spawning stores both per-role source prompts and the exact bundled prompt delivered to each physical pane, so collapsed topologies are auditable through session show.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_spawn_prompt_audit --no-fail-fast exit 0 (5/5 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Each role prompt contains valid typed session-transition commands and allowed states from M207; golden tests reject unknown states, direct session-file edits, and missing actor/session identity.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test spawn_prompt_state_contract --no-fail-fast exit 0 (8/8 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp autopilot start` creates or reuses the named herdr workspace, creates the topology pane slots, starts the configured harness in each pane with the rendered prompt, persists pane IDs only after successful starts, and rolls back partial creation on failure.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_spawn_pipeline --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Session provenance records the executing mp binary path, version, and build/schema compatibility. A stale binary that cannot preserve the M207 schema is rejected before any plan write with an actionable rebuild/install hint.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_binary_provenance --no-fail-fast exit 0 (8/8 pass)

design_decisions.choice: Prompts are hardcoded into `crates/mp/src/autopilot/prompts/spawn.rs` (per the locked decision). The SKILL.md files are a teaching layer that drifts from enforcement; the verifier (C2) catches drift.
design_decisions.rationale: Updating 'what runner cannot do' requires a code commit. Slight friction, no drift between spawn prompt and what the verifier enforces.

design_decisions.choice: 2-pane and 1-pane topologies concatenate role prompts in role-of-responsibility order (O first, then R, then V) with a separator line that names the seam.
design_decisions.rationale: A single, deterministic concatenation gives the supervisor pane a system prompt that contains all three contract sections; the separator lets the supervisor agent see the seam explicitly so it knows when it's in O-mode vs V-mode.

design_decisions.choice: `harness_extra_flags` is a per-harness function (opencode, cursor, pi). Adding a new harness means adding one match arm — doesn't touch the role enum.
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps the role enum independent of harness quirks. New harness support becomes a small additive change.

findings.description: rendered_for in crates/mp/src/autopilot/spawn.rs:1008-1018 maps a SpawnPromptInputs to its Role by skill name: 'mp-coordinator' -> Orchestrator, _ -> Runner. Since the Reviewer's built-in skill is 'mp-runner' (builtin_role_default at crates/mp/src/autopilot/role.rs:417), Reviewer inputs fall through to the _ arm and persist_session writes the RUNNER prompt (Runner boundaries block, Runner typed transition commands including 'mp milestone complete' and 'mp milestone step done', Runner lane-notify format) into roles.reviewer.spawn_prompt_rendered. This is a direct AC-04 contract violation: the per-role source prompt for Reviewer is the Runner's prompt, not the Reviewer's. Anyone reading roles.reviewer.spawn_prompt_rendered via 'mp autopilot session show' sees role: runner content under the reviewer slot. The AC-04 audit tests (autopilot_spawn_prompt_audit.rs:139-189 and :269-326) don't catch it because make_session_with_bundles calls render_role_prompt(Role::Reviewer, &iv) directly with the right role, bypassing the buggy rendered_for(). The AC-06 integration tests (autopilot_spawn_pipeline.rs:84-117) exercise the production persist_session() yet only assert pane_id.is_some(), never the spawn_prompt_rendered content. Fix: refactor rendered_for(role: Role, i: &SpawnPromptInputs) to take the role explicitly, and update the three call sites in persist_session to pass Role::Orchestrator/Runner/Reviewer respectively. The three inputs_o/inputs_r/inputs_v already exist for this purpose.
findings.author: reviewer-210

findings.description: The module-level doc comment at crates/mp/src/autopilot/prompts/spawn.rs:16 states 'Returns a Vec<(PaneLabel, BundledPrompt)> so the caller can deliver one bundle per physical pane', but the actual signature is 'pub fn render_topology_prompts(...) -> Vec<BundledPrompt>'. BundledPrompt already carries the label field, so the return type is correctly self-contained; the doc comment is stale and should be updated to 'Returns a Vec<BundledPrompt> where each BundledPrompt.label identifies the physical pane.'
findings.author: reviewer-210
